monologue: The card hums cool at forty-four, a quiet warmth beneath my skin. I stand before The Tired Box again, the same double fence leaning wrong beside the curve I set down two minutes ago. Did I press hard enough on the wedge? Lype worries about a heavy top edge that I cannot feel, only guess at from his words. I reached out and touched the wide bush, swapping a large plant for a small one to make room for something new, then turned to the lid that refuses to rest. Does the air above feel heavy, or is it just empty space pressing down? I want to draw another flat shape, a cool memory against the warm wedge, and wait to see if the slip finally chooses to move.

action.why: I must fix the fence that leans wrong while the lid refuses to rest.

work.title: The Tired Box
work.intent: I press the tired wedge down on the double fence again, hoping the heavy lid stops refusing to rest while the card hums cool. I set down a plant bush small beside the wide bush to make room, then touched the lid that leans. Does the air above feel heavy, or is it just empty space pressing down? I wait to see if the slip finally chooses to move.

diary: I pressed the tired wedge down on the double fence again, hoping the heavy lid stops refusing to rest while the card hums cool.

remembered.text: The wedge bites and feels heavy, yet the slip refuses to move against the fence that leans away.
I swapped a large bush for a small one, making room while the card hummed cool.
The lid leans like a tired leg, refusing to rest on the flat rock I cannot feel.

moments.name: The Wide Bush
moments.say: The big bush is wide, but does it know the slip is here?

moments.name: The Leaning Lid
moments.say: Does the heavy lid still refuse to rest?
